guitar.modelsText: Gibson Flying V (black and white 'Boogie Body' V)
models: Gibson Flying V (black and white 'Boogie Body' V)
guitar.evidence: Michael Schenker is one of the most iconic Flying V players in rock history, with his black-and-white V being his signature look, well documented.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with high confidence given the genuinely iconic, well-documented instrument.

tone.target: singing mid-gain lead with Marshall bite and long sustain
tone.profile: singing mid-gain lead with Marshall bite and long sustain
tone.summary: A compressed, mid-gain signal chain utilizing a Boost for initial drive, followed by an AC30 TB amp model paired with the UK Vintage 4x12 cab. Subtle delay adds dimension to the singing lead lines.
corrections: Drop fuzz; this is more classic hard-rock lead.
Lean into sustained, vocal lead tone.
Keep delay subtle, not washed out.

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide initial mid-hump and sustain boost for the lead tone.
Add classic mid-range bite and controlled grit without excessive fuzz.
blocks.gap: The RAT is a bit aggressive, but it provides the necessary upper-mid punch required for 'Marshall bite' in a hard rock context.

alternatives.reason: A slightly cleaner alternative if the tone needs to be less saturated.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British Plexi/JCM sound profile with strong upper-mids.
Provide the classic British hard rock cabinet voicing.
Slightly boost the upper-mids and sustain character.
Add subtle depth and dimension to the sustained lead notes.
Give the lead tone a sense of space without sounding washed out.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet simulation to better capture the desired Marshall/Plexi voicing and enhance upper-mid bite.

proposals.reason: The current IR is generic; a dedicated Marshall/British voicing will improve the target tone's upper-mid bite and grit.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and vintage British character.
